q: This study explored whether AI IDEs with agentic capabilities can produce end-to-end largescale software systems and what design issues those systems exhibit.
r: Include: Cursor agentic IDE generates 10 large-scale projects from requirements and evaluates functionality and design quality, project-level code development.

q: AI coding agents are increasingly integrated into real-world software development workflows, yet their robustness under diverse and adversarial scenarios remains poorly understood.
r: EC6: fuzzing for behavioural anomalies of agent CLIs (robustness/behaviour), not evaluation of code-development tasks.

q: PaperCoder, a multi-agent LLM framework that transforms machine learning papers into operational code repositories.
r: EC5: main contribution is a new agent (PaperCoder) for ML paper-to-code, a specialised domain, with nothing for evaluation method.

q: This critical scoping review maps 348 studies and applies a five-step interpretation procedure to 94 comparison and diagnostic records from 42 studies
r: IC1: scoping review of component replacement in general LLM agents, not coding agents or software development tasks.

q: Fine-tuning on just 145 of these trajectories improves cross-lingual performance from 1.6% to 3.6% on SWE-bench Multilingual.
r: EC6: SWE-bench style issue-repair benchmark and training data, always excluded.

q: We introduce Code Primitives, reusable software components that adapt their implementations, interfaces, and dependencies to target repositories, and LEGO, a framework that retrieves, coordinates, and verifies these primitives during repository construction.
r: EC5: main contribution is a new technique (Code Primitives, LEGO) evaluated on its own and external benchmarks, not an evaluation method.

q: Our findings suggest that skill libraries for coding agents should be treated not only as retrievable resources, but also as controllable, verifiable, and recoverable execution abstractions.
r: Include: skill libraries (context mechanism) for coding agents, evaluated on cost, success and process metrics.

q: WebViSE transforms design knowledge embedded in source websites into reusable Visual Skills and transfers this visual design intelligence to Website Generators.
r: IC1: skills for LLM website generators (visual design), not clearly coding agents; doubt excludes.
